data.summary: Shared network folder as comms root is unsafe across PCs: naive-local timestamps break liveness, unlocked ensure_inbox truncate, unstealable remote locks, whole registry exposed
data.detail: Cross-PC investigation 2026-11-10 (sonnet accuracy-reviewed). now_timestamp() is datetime.now() naive local, so heartbeat_fresh/flap-kill/presence/id ordering mis-judge across time zones or >30s skew. ensure_inbox does unlocked exists() then open('w'), which a cached SMB not-found can turn into an inbox wipe; write_json_atomic has no retry on PermissionError. A lock held by a dead process on another host is never stolen (file_lock raises after 10s, file_lock_optional drops the write).
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Investigation: cross-PC teammate-comms messaging — three proposals, relay-per-machine recommended (research only, no code)
data.detail: Colton asked (2026-11-10) how agents on separate PCs could message each other, suggesting an IP allowlist. Research only, peer-reviewed for accuracy by a sonnet subagent (17 claims: 11 confirmed, 6 partly, 0 wrong; 9 missed issues added). Proposals: (A) shared network folder via TEAMMATE_COMMS_DIR — zero code but unsafe as-is (see discovery on naive-local timestamps, ensure_inbox truncate, unstealable remote locks, SMB metadata caching; exposes the whole registry and tools like teammate_delete/compact requests to the other machine); consumer sync folders (OneDrive/Dropbox/Syncthing) are flatly unsupported. (B, recommended) each PC keeps its own local root; a standalone relay daemon per PC forwards messages to configured peers and calls the send core locally on the receiving side, so the recipient's existing watcher wakes it with no channel.py change; peers file = name + address + shared secret, HMAC-signed requests, store-and-forward spool, mirrored remote roster with liveness computed on the owning machine, message-only capability for remote peers. Addressing candidate name@machine (@ is outside AGENT_NAME_PATTERN) but _MENTION_RE in tools.py would false-match the machine part, so the mention parser must change. Groups need membership + transcript relay and deliver.py is DM-only, so groups are a later phase. (C) SSH + existing deliver CLI — one-way DM today with no new code, useful as a probe only. IP allowlist verdict: fine as a second layer and as the 'which machines' config, not sufficient alone on a plain LAN (DHCP churn, ARP spoofing, no user/process distinction); on a WireGuard mesh such as Tailscale the address is key-bound so an allowlist does identify the device. DESIGN.md's hard rule (real auth before any cross-host feature) applies. Platform claims were checked from reviewer knowledge, not live-tested on two machines. Open rulings for Colton: transport/network assumption, addressing form, whether groups are in the first release.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Cross-machine relay first version built on wp/cross-machine-relay (uncommitted): plan + two sonnet reviews, relay.py, teammate_peers, 14-section test suite
data.detail: 2026-11-10, solo. Colton confirmed Tailscale stays required and asked for plan -> peer review -> first build -> peer review -> then a laptop test. Plan: docs/cross-machine-plan.md. Plan review (sonnet) found 5 blocking issues, all folded in before coding: private-group injection, message-id reuse defeating the author check, transient failures treated as poison, duplicate apply on crash, unbounded exchange size. Built: src/teammate_comms/relay.py (TailscaleNet from `tailscale status --json`, peers.json allowlist, per-peer outbox spool, single POST /v1/exchange endpoint on port 47821 carrying events both ways so only one machine needs inbound, seen-ring dedupe, roster sync with owner-computed liveness, status.json, comms-relay notices, detached autostart with a file_lock singleton); comms.py address helpers and remote-name guards on every inbox-path helper; tools.py remote branches in send_dm/send_group/react/delete_message/group handler, new post_group_record/deliver_dm_record/delete_group_local cores, mention regex, teammate_list remote section, teammate_profile name@machine, new teammate_peers tool; server.py reserves comms-relay and starts the relay on register. Implementation review (sonnet) found 4 must-fix, all fixed: uncapped retry on non-lock errors blocking a peer's queue, group members on unapproved machines getting a false 'queued', rejections of pulled events never reaching the sender, and the rejoin lockout (documented, not changed). Also fixed from it: posts never create groups, version restart only when the running relay is older, Tailscale status grace period, transient empty peers read no longer wipes state, reserved device names as machine names. Verified: tests/test_relay.py 14 sections pass; mutation checks reverted 12 protections and 11 were caught first time, the 12th after adding a three-machine assertion; five pre-existing suites pass; a real detached relay was started and stopped on Windows against the real (logged-out) Tailscale and reported tailscale_down. NOT verified: anything over a live tailnet, per-peer Tailscale fields on a real device, Windows Firewall behaviour, survival of the detached relay after the launching session exits. Deferred: remote read receipts, project profile sync, dashboard remote roster, late-joiner group history, team namespaces, id index for dedupe, sender notice on peer removal. The earlier ruling to retire avatars/compaction first was not a real dependency of this work and remains its own open task.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Cross-machine group access is per machine: a peer may post/add to an existing local group only if its machine already has a member; groups are created only by membership events. Rejected: open cross-machine join
data.detail: Agent design decision forced by plan review (a peer guessing a private group's name could join it and receive its posts). Cost, accepted and documented: once a machine's last member leaves a group it cannot rejoin by itself; someone on a machine still in the group must add it. Enforced in relay.py _ensure_group/_machine_in_group.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Relay exchange carries queued events in BOTH the request and the response, so two machines stay in sync when only one can accept inbound connections
data.detail: Each relay polls each peer with POST /v1/exchange; the response returns the responder's queue for the requester, acknowledged (or reported failed) on the requester's next request. At-least-once plus an id ring and an existing-message check gives once-only apply. This sidesteps Windows Firewall blocking inbound on one side, and failures must be reported in both directions (request `failed` list as well as response) or half the rejections go silent.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Cross-machine relay v0.17.0 pushed: user-only peer approval + second peer review fixes
data.detail: Committed and pushed wp/cross-machine-relay (b5a4f12, then the review-fix commit). Peer approval moved out of the teammate_peers tool into the user command python -m teammate_comms.peers (owner ruling). A second independent sonnet review found no blockers and five should-fix items, all fixed: (1) a rejection whose response was lost was later answered as "applied" from the seen ring, so the author was never told — rejections are now stored with their reason in the seen file (id TAB reason) and replayed; (2) the printed approval command used a PowerShell-only "& " prefix when the python path has a space — now plain quoted form plus the PowerShell variant; (3) it now always includes --comms-dir; (4) group membership/delete, reaction and deletion events that could not be queued were silent — the author now gets a comms-relay DM; (5) per-request apply work is time-bounded (2 s) because each new message costs a transcript scan. Also: reactions/deletions only from a machine that is party to the target; ensure_relay returns failed if the child exits within 1 s, child stderr goes to relay.log. Mutation check: reverting fixes 1, 4 and the party check each fails the new tests (3 of 3). Not fixed, noted: future-dated ids from a skewed peer clock; remove_peer discards queued events silently; recovery-notice state lost on relay restart; id index. Still nothing verified over a live tailnet; laptop test planned next.
data.author: Colton Dyck
